verdict.what: a tiered pagoda-style watchtower with a copper spire
verdict.style: medieval fantasy, Japanese pagoda crossed with timber-framed Tudor
verdict.looks: A square tower of about five stacked tiers. The base is a tall plinth of grey stone brick and cobblestone with green moss patches and a small dark wooden door, flanked by lanterns. Above it, a dark oak storey with white plaster infill panels and timber posts, then a wide dark oak overhanging eave with a stepped edge. A second oak-and-white-plaster storey with lanterns hanging on chains follows, then a dark oak balcony ledge with small fence posts, and a further oak storey with white panels. The top is a steep pyramidal roof in oxidised teal copper blocks, with a thin antenna pole at the tip. A few copper-brown cubes sit on the roof edge and near one corner, some looking like deliberate ornaments and one or two looking loose. Orange glowing lamp blocks show in the upper storeys.
verdict.summary: A well-proportioned tiered watchtower whose mossy stone base, oak eaves, plaster infill and teal copper spire read as one coherent medieval-pagoda style; it only needs the loose copper cubes on the roof edge either tied in or removed and a bit of trim before it is placeable.
